sources.entry: Chatwoot | Customer support platform with live chat, email and social inboxes

summary.one_liner: Chatwoot is an open-source, self-hosted customer support platform that centralizes live chat, email, and social channel conversations into one inbox, positioned as an alternative to Intercom and Zendesk.
summary.what_it_does: Chatwoot combines multi-channel conversations (website live chat, email, Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, WhatsApp, Telegram, Line, SMS) into a single support inbox. It includes an AI agent called Captain that automates responses to common queries, and a built-in Help Center portal for publishing articles and FAQs. Team tools cover private notes, @mentions, labels, canned responses, auto-assignment, business hours, teams, and automation. Contact management includes profiles, segments, custom attributes, pre-chat forms, and campaigns. Integrations named in the README are Slack, Dialogflow, Shopify, Google Translate, Linear, and Dashboard Apps, and reporting covers live view, conversation/agent/inbox/label/team reports, CSAT, and downloadable reports.
use_cases: shared inbox for website chat and email
omnichannel customer messaging across WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook
public help center and FAQ portal
customer satisfaction (CSAT) reporting for support teams
how_to_run: Deploy with the Heroku one-click deploy button linked in the README (set environment variables per the linked guide)
Deploy as a DigitalOcean 1-Click Kubernetes app
See the deployment page referenced in the README for other supported options
notable: Open-source, self-hosted alternative to Intercom, Zendesk and Salesforce Service Cloud, per the README
Captain AI agent for automating routine support replies
Single inbox across live chat, email, and many social and messaging channels
Built-in Help Center portal for self-service articles
Uses git-flow branching with develop as base branch and master or v1.x.x tags for stable releases
caveats: Heroku deployment may break features unless the relevant environment variables are set correctly, per the README
Deployment beyond the listed one-click options requires following the separate deployment page
The README does not state a self-hosting hardware or resource requirement
keywords: manage customer conversations in one place
